title: Regional routing resilience: latency pinning, capacity-aware steering, and circuit-breaker playbook
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem statement: As Redwood scales across regions we see intermittent cross-region tail latency and hot-pool saturation that causes SLO violations for latency-sensitive hosted API customers. We need a clear, operable routing policy and circuit breaker behavior that preserves customer SLOs while maximizing successful request completion and minimizing waste (cost and duplicated work).

Goals: 1) Define latency-based routing with hysteresis to avoid flapping; 2) Add geo-pinning for user/regulatory constraints; 3) Implement capacity-aware steering so overloaded regions shed or offload traffic gracefully; 4) Specify circuit-breaker triggers and fallback routes; 5) Provide testing plan, SLO/alerting deltas, and a rollback/playbook for incidents.

Design summary: - Latency-based routing: compute a moving 90th/95th percentile per-region for each logical route (model+route) over a 60s window. Prefer regions meeting target_p95_latency * 1.2 headroom. Only switch primary region when delta > 20% for two consecutive windows (hysteresis). - Soft geo-pinning: allow customers to opt into strong geo-pin. For non-pinned customers, routing may prefer a region but still allow low-volume cross-region fallthrough for availability. For pinned tenants we only route within allowed regions. - Capacity-aware steering: expose two capacity signals per region: available_inference_slots (instant) and expected_utilization_tail (30s forecast). If available_inference_slots < threshold_low (e.g., 15% free) mark region as "soft-constrained"; if < threshold_critical (e.g., 5% free) mark as "hard-constrained". Soft-constrained regions accept low-latency traffic but may probabilistically shed best-effort requests (e.g., long-chained streaming, non-interactive batch). Hard-constrained regions trigger routing away plus circuit-breaker for new long-running requests. - Circuit breakers: define breakers per (customer, route, region) with three trip criteria: latency_budget_exhaustion, error_rate_spike, and slot-starvation. On trip: immediate short-circuit to fallback region variant for retry with exponential backoff and per-client rate-limits to avoid thundering herds. Breakers auto-recover after cool-down and/or manual reset. - Load shedding: implement prioritized token buckets on the edge to drop or downgrade lower-priority work (info/watermark responses, background evals) first. Provide a graceful degrade option that returns a fast 503 with Retry-After and optional partial output.

Operational hooks: - Metrics: per-region p50/p90/p95 latency, queue depth, slot utilisation, circuit-breaker state counts, dropped_request_count, rerouted_request_count. - Alerts: SLO breach shadow when reroute percentage > 10% for 5m; circuit-breakers tripped > 1% of new requests in 5m. - Dashboard: per-tenant routing path visualizer, heatmap of region constraints, and a per-model steering table.

Deployment plan: 1) Feature-flag the routing controller in Canary region; 2) Run closed loop with synthetic traffic and chaos (partial AZ outages, induced high tail) for 72h; 3) Enable capacity signals from Dedicated pools (integration work noted in dependencies); 4) Soft rollout to 10% of production traffic with telemetry capture; 5) 100% rollout if no regressions for 48h.

Testing & validation: - Unit tests for hysteresis windowing and capacity state machine. - Integration test: small multi-region cluster with load generator to validate routing decision distribution and that pinned customers never leave allowed regions. - Chaos scenarios: network partitions, region flapping, sudden drop in available slots. Run through incident playbook to ensure circuit-breakers behave as expected.

Acceptance criteria: - Controller selects target region within 120ms decision time under normal load. - When a region is marked hard-constrained, 95% of new interactive requests are routed away within 10s. - No SLO regressions (p95 increases <= 5%) for tenants routed by the new controller during 10% canary. - Observability: alerts firing and dashboard shows reroute and breaker state.

Notes: This ticket focuses on policy and controller behavior. Implementation of the slot exporter and Dedicated pool hooks is tracked separately. Coordinate with Networking team on edge token-bucket changes and with Console team for dashboard surfaces.

acceptance_criteria: Routing controller respects geo-pin flags and never routes pinned tenants outside allowed regions.
Soft-constrained regions probabilistically shed lower-priority traffic; hard-constrained regions trigger immediate routing away for new long-lived requests.
Circuit-breaker state is visible in metrics and can be reset via Console.
No >5% p95 regression for canary customers after 48h at 10% traffic exposure.
notes: Prefer incremental rollout. Keep policy simple initially — tune thresholds with real telemetry. Ensure playbook includes manual override to pin traffic to a region during incident investigations.
